CRITICAL_CAVEAT: This file describes UI-INTENDED transitions only (what buttons/pages exist and who can see them). It is NOT a server-enforced contract. The single generic write endpoint PATCH /api/bff/tasks/{task_id} (app/routers/bff_write.py:1077-1112) is used to actually perform every status change in this file, and it performs ZERO role/authorization checks and ZERO from-state validation -- it only checks that the target 'status' value is a member of the 9 known values or a recognized legacy alias (app/routers/bff_write.py:1090-1095, using app/helpers/task_status.py:16-32). Therefore ANY authenticated actor (any role) can, by calling the API directly (bypassing the UI), set ANY task to ANY of the 9 statuses regardless of the 'allowed_roles' listed below. This mirrors the structural gap already reported in cmd_118 finding #3 (score_be app/routers/bff_write.py:1456-1486 POST /api/bff/qc/approve has no get_actor_role()/is_qc_delegated() call) -- that gap in fact extends to every write endpoint listed in this file (post_asset_upload, post_qc_notify_existing, post_retakes, post_qc_approve_bff, patch_task all share the same pattern: Depends(get_actor_id) only, never Depends(get_actor_role) or is_qc_delegated()).
